claims.text: Tx focuses on the cause, esp alleviating or moderating hypoxia.
claims.quote: Treatment of cor pulmonale is difficult; it focuses on the cause (see table Causes of Heart Failure), particularly alleviation or moderation of hypoxia.
claims.locator: Treatment of Right Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale

claims.text: Acute or critical illness: cautious diuresis, inotropic support (eg, milrinone) and pulmonary vasodilation (if not contraindicated) may help.
claims.quote: Cautious diuresis, inotropic support with agents such as milrinone, and pulmonary vasodilation (in the absence of contraindications) may be helpful.
claims.locator: Treatment of Right Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale › Acute or critical illness

claims.text: Pulmonary vasodilators: generally not effective for causes other than select group 1 PAH;
claims.quote: Pulmonary vasodilators (eg, hydralazine, calcium channel blockers, nitrous oxide, prostacyclin analogs, phosphodiesterase inhibitors), although beneficial in select Group 1 (primary) pulmonary arterial hypertension patients, are generally not effective for other causes of cor pulmonale.
claims.locator: Treatment of Right Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale

claims.text: not typically indicated for cor pulmonale from chronic lung disease, but may have a role in severe cases.
claims.quote: Pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapies, including pulmonary vasodilators, are not typically indicated for cor pulmonale due to chronic lung disease, although they may play a role in severe cases
claims.locator: Treatment of Right Heart Failure and Cor Pulmonale
